name: multi-user-synthetic
description: Multi-user linear bandit: 5 instances of 100 users in 5 clusters, 500 actions in R^10, 20 random actions offered per step (as in CLUB and SCLUB), 2 runs each. LinUCB shared, per user, and per user with k-means clusters (5 clusters), against CLUB and SCLUB. Theoretical defaults.

policies.label: LinUCB
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: LinUCB_IND_KMeans
notes: lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

policies.label: CLUB
notes: alpha=1.0 (exploration weight, tuned on the data in the paper)
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)
cluster_alpha=2.0 (tuned on the data in the paper)

policies.label: SCLUB
notes: cluster_alpha: 4 R sqrt(d / lambda_x), lambda_x from the actions offered
lambda_=0.1 (any lambda > 0 keeps the bound valid)

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Paper values: alpha=1 for LinUCB, LinUCB_IND, LinUCB_IND_KMeans and SCLUB. Safe in theory, but they often explore too much.
notices.todo: Grid search: param_grid=True. Or set them, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: K-means users (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_IND_KMeans pulls each user model towards its k-means cluster. No regret guarantee.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret, action of every step, peak memory. The charts cannot show them.

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Between two stored points, the curve is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=50.

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: Runs in parallel (n_jobs=4), one BLAS thread each.
notices.todo: Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
